issue.title: fix: values in library subcharts are ignored

labels.name: size/XS
labels.description: Denotes a PR that changes 0-9 lines, ignoring generated files.

issue.body:
Signed-off-by: Alberto Garcia <albgp22@gmail.com>

closes #10899

Since helm v3.8.2 was released, values imports from library subcharts via import-values stopped working. This bug has also been reported by other collegues as you can see in the linked issue.

This PR solves this problem, reverting a change included in [this commit](https://github.com/helm/helm/commit/5d017e11f1f47345a3559bf70f63d81a7edc981a) which changed value precedence.

body: @albgp22 any reason why you closed #10940? Did it not address this issue?

Hi @bacongobbler. It did address this issue, but then I saw that this fix would introduce the bug reported in [#9940](https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/9940) again. I will try to come up with a solution as soon as I have time, but in the meantime any help from helm contributors is really appreciated.

We had the same suprise as well regarding the change. Would be great to hear from the maintainers if as you @albgp22  stated: "Imported values from libraries overriding the ones in the application values.yaml file was the expected and logical behavior." In any case this should not be changed in a patch version.
@mattfarina what is your opinion on this?
We are actually enjoying that https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/9940 is finally fixed. When considering a fix, please ensure that this does not return.

issue.title: import-values from sub charts are not working since 3.8.2
issue.body:
As described in documentation, we can import values from sub charts into parent chart:

```
# child's values.yaml file

exports:
  data:
    image:
      repository: busybox
```

```
# parent's Chart.yaml file
apiVersion: v2
name: test
description: A Helm chart for Kubernetes
type: application
version: 0.1.0
appVersion: "1.16.0"

dependencies:
  - name: child
    repository: "file://charts/child"
    version: 1.0.0
    tags:
      - child
    import-values:
      - data
```

```
# parent's values.yaml file
image:
  repository: nginx
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  tag: ""
```

Before version v3.8.2 we had the following output:

helm upgrade -i test . --set tags.child=true --dry-run --debug

```
COMPUTED VALUES:
child:
  exports:
    data:
      image:
        pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        repository: busybox
        tag: ""
  global: {}
image:
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  repository: busybox
  tag: ""
```

As you can see the image was changed in parent chart, but if we'll try the same with version >=v3.8.2:
```
COMPUTED VALUES:
child:
  exports:
    data:
      image:
        repository: busybox
  global: {}
image:
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  repository: nginx
  tag: ""
```

I can't understand what was changed and how to achieve the same in last version of helm?

Output of `helm version`: version.BuildInfo{Version:"v3.9.0", GitCommit:"7ceeda6c585217a19a1131663d8cd1f7d641b2a7", GitTreeState:"clean", GoVersion:"go1.18.2"}

Output of `kubectl version`: Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"24", GitVersion:"v1.24.1", GitCommit:"3ddd0f45aa91e2f30c70734b175631bec5b5825a", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2022-05-24T12:17:11Z", GoVersion:"go1.18.2", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/arm64"}

Cloud Provider/Platform (AKS, GKE, Minikube etc.): AWS EKS

issue.title: Introduce import-values strategy + revert default strategy for backwards compat

labels.name: size/L
labels.description: Denotes a PR that changes 100-499 lines, ignoring generated files.

labels.name: needs-rebase
labels.description: Indicates a PR cannot be merged because it has merge conflicts with HEAD.

issue.body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Make sure to read the Contributing Guide before submitting your PR: https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
2. If this PR closes another issue, add 'closes #<issue number>' somewhere in the PR summary. GitHub will automatically close that issue when this PR gets merged. Alternatively, adding 'refs #<issue number>' will not close the issue, but help provide the reviewer more context.-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
With the introduction of a bug fix https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/9940 https://github.com/helm/helm/commit/5d017e11f1f47345a3559bf70f63d81a7edc981a there was a breaking introduced that makes it no longer possible to import values from a sub-chart that override values that are already defined in the importing chart. This issue is described in https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/10899

Between the original behavior and the one that "fixed" there are two possible scenarios for a string value:
1. override: import values from the sub-chart and override everything in the parent chart (old behavior)
2. ifNotPresent: import values from the sub-chart and only import the value if it's not defined in the chart chart (current behavior since the "fix")

Something else I noticed is that the ifNotPresent behavior was already applied to an import-values entry with child and parent paths before, so it was not consistently implemented even before the "fix". Even though the helm docs mention "override" behavior.

| Type | Original behavior | Since "fix" | With PR | [Docs](https://helm.sh/docs/topics/charts/) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| string | override | ifNotPresent | override | override  (not explicitly mentioned, but I assume the same as child + parent path) |
| child + parent path | ifNotPresent | ifNotPresent | ifNotPresent | override |

So the aim of this PR is to revert the breaking changes, which should happen at major versions. And additionally introduce a "strategy" to explictly define the behavior (naming can still be discussed). Adding the strategy looks at follows:
```
# alternative for string with a different strategy
dependencies:
  - name: child
    import-values:
      - key: data
        strategy: override
```
```
# child + parent path with a strategy
dependencies:
  - name: child
    import-values:
      - child: default.data
        parent: myimports
        strategy: ifNotPresent
```

A few todos/questions:
- [ ] does the json spec of Chart.yaml need to updated somewhere? I wasn't able to find it in the repo.
- [ ] if desired for short term, we could just revert to the "fix PR" and you can use child + parent path instead
- [ ] docs will need to be adjusted, unless we want to change the default behavior of child + parent path from ifNotPresent to override to reflect the docs?
- [ ] expand unit tests?

Closes https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/10899

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**If applicable**:
- [ ] this PR contains documentation
- [x] this PR contains unit tests
- [ ] this PR has been tested for backwards compatibility

body:
There are so many cases in which a strange/odd behavior has not been considered a bug as if doing like that the new Helm release would introduce a non-backward compatible change (so breaking those deployment workflows expecting the current behavior) and so, in those cases, it was proposed to solve it as a new feature (e.g. proposing to add some new input param to the helm command in order to get the new desired behavior without breaking compatibility).

I think not following this approach for #9440  was a mistake and so it would be good to solve it in a coming release, doing as @Cybermaxke  comments above (i.e., to get the behavior implemented by #9440 as a new feature to be triggered by some additional input param passed to the helm install/upgrade command and/or additional Chart.yaml field asking for it).

It looks PR #11162 is waiting for being accepted/merged to "main" for some long time.
Is there anything preventing it to happen?
We are not able to upgrade Helm from 3.8.1 to any newer release due to the NBC introduced by 3.8.2 on imported-values behavior; it looks we are not the only ones "suffering" this problem.

Asking in order to understand if not accepting (yet) that PR #11162 is only because Helm guys allowed to accept it are overloaded ... or is it because they see some "issues/problems" on accepting this PR (?).

Thanks in advance.

Responded in the PR.

PS. I'm not a core maintainer, I just help with issues.

@bacongobbler , @mattfarina could you comment?
I think we should revert the non-backward-compatible (NBC) change introduced in Helm behavior from 3.8.2 onwards (because of the merged PR closing #9940) as soon as possible.
The proposed PR #1162 for that is still providing a solution for the people asking for a different behavior, so when this PR being merged we will

- get again the previous behavior (so solving the NBC introduced from 3.8.2)
- giving a solution (based on a new helm input param) for the people asking for a new behavior

We (and some others) are blocking the upgrade (in our deployment pipelines) to newer Helm versions because of this introduced NBC from 3.8.2
